E. Cape EMS Disaster

By: Sinethemba Nogude | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Its in rural areas where communities lament the lack of emergency service, being forced to resort to undignified means in order to save lives.

Unique Selling Point:
We take a ride along with underresourced and understaffed EMS workers in the province, as they try to save lives despite these simingly insurmountable obstacles. EMS Mzamane Mgwantashe gives us a glimpse into the lives of long-suffering EMS workers.

Summary:
EMS workers have embarked on a strike recentlytThe unprotected strike is affecting EMS services mainly in the rural areas of the Amathole District where desperate villagers now have to pool their resources to hire private cars to get to healthcare facilities.

Poor access to EMS is a longstanding problem in many rural areas in the Eastern Cape. The situation triggered the South African Human Rights Commission (SAHRC) in 2015 to investigate and produce a report with detailed recommendations.

But, in her recent budget speech, Health MEC Nomakhosazana Meth acknowledged that the Eastern Cape Department of Health has not yet addressed the gaps identified by the SAHRC.

Meth says the department should have at least 650 ambulances, but currently, it has 447, of which 181 are patient transport vehicles, and 41 are rescue vehicles. She said this falls short of the recommended one ambulance per 10,000 population. The department had 2,244 EMS staff against a population of about 6.5 million, as there is a shortage of intermediate life-support personnel.
This leaves many rural communities isolated and no way to access emergency medical services.We speak to these communities that feel they have been left to fend for themselves

Mzamane Mgwantshe

Script : Eastern Cape EMS

[Kendrick extraction] It not there [ Mac and Mzamane checking ambulance]
[Headblocks] They aren’t here
Upsound Mzsamane: The oxygen tank, small and large are not here
Mac : So a basic thing like oxygen is not here, and thats obviously important if someone is in danger.
Mzamane: You Open the windows, so that the person can get air.

V/O This is the shocking state of ambulances that are meant to serve 7-million people in the Eastern Cape. In town after town, village after village, people tell us the same story: no ambulances.
Link with the drone: Access to Emergency Medical care and Medical Health Care is enshrined in our constitution, but it seems for many in rural parts of the Eastern Cape, these rights do not apply…IF THE CUT CAN’T BE MADE SMOOTHER BRING BACK THE WORDS
V/O Xhora-mouth on the Wild Coast is about as remote as you can find - with East London a four-hour drive south … Mthatha a hundred kilometres north.
V/O The availability of an ambulance here can become a matter of life and death.
Upsound Nosintu: 00:00:24 This is not a good place. We are starving because we have to pay for private transport
V/O Nosintu Ntenteni grew up here and in September last year she really needed an ambulance…she was about to have her first child.
Upsound Nosintu : I first called the ambulance and it didn't come I didn’t even know I was in labor - my waist was painful, it was around 12pm the evening. I gave birth at 3am in the morning. I wrapped the baby.
V/O She still needed to get to a hospital - over an hour’s drive away.
Upsound Nosintu I called a taxi driver called Babalo, they got here at 7 am .I only got to the hospital around 8 am.
Upsound Phumzile Msaro : You can imagine on our dirt roads, and someone is pregnant and bumping on the back of the bakkie…and some give birth at the back of bakkies.
V/O Community leader Phumzile Msaro has been part of a desperate struggle to bring medical services here.
Upsound Phumzile Msaro: In 2013 We went all the way to East London…The Human rights commission panel was there, we explained how life is critical here. The human rights commission did a report it tells you what is supposed to be done. I can tell you none of them has happened.
V/O The 2015 HRC report detailed the shocking state of EMS for the province’s rural communities and recommended improving the condition of the ambulance fleet and their response.an d sai
Upsound Phumzile: People are dying whilst there are ambulances that are supposed to come and there is no hope.
V/O Over 300 km inland at Fort Beaufort I meet Mzamane Mgwantashe. A pasisonate? EMS worker for over 7 years, Mzamane risked dismissal speaking to us, because for him, the situation has become unbearable.
UpsoundMzamane EMS worker : 08:12 The community is suffering because the ambulance does not have the equipment and we have been trying. We are covering 120 villages with 2 ambulances
Mac: have you ever been in a position where you had to help someone and you didnt have equipment.Can you tell me what happened?
Upsound Mzamane EMS worker: There was a call that came in from Victoria to East London transferring patients…They didn’t have an oxygen tank….and the patient died on the way because there was no oxygen
Upsound Rolene : We've tried to prioritize EMS services and do the best we can with the resources at our disposal.
V/O Throughout the years, the Eastern Cape Department of Health has been dogged by maladministration and corruption…repeatedly coming close to collapse. Appointed a year ago, the new head of department Doctor Roelene Wagner says they’re barely getting by.
Upsound Rolene Roelene Wagner: Across the years, the budget allocations to the Health Department in the Eastern Cape has decreased. There are 447 vehicles that we have within our fleet within those we have around 324 that are operational now, even if you have an operational ambulance you need sufficient crew to man the ambulances We have just over 2200 staff.
V/O The National Department of Health’s Standards for Emergency Medical Services make it clear that Ambulances should be adequately equipped at all times, but it's seldom the case here.
Mzamane EMS worker: This is the only checklist we used to use, it’s the state of the vehicle on this side, and the equipment that should be here on this side, for example, a trauma board Its here. The oxygen tanks, small and large are not here, this is where the oxygen is supposed to be. There is no stretcher.
Mac : Suction Unit ?
Upsound Mzamane EMS woker We are improvising you see, that is why we manage.
Mac : But Mzamane you cant improvise oxygen, opening windows does not help.
Mac : And when we have cases of woman giving birth ?
Upsound Mzamane : If they, unfortunately, give birth on the way, you can’t cut the umbilical cord because you don’t have surgical blades because you don’t have a maternity pack, It’s either they cut it at the hospital or you use what you have.
Mac : When spoke to some of the workers,Some of the ambulances that they've been given do not have equipment. I mean, a simple thing like an oxygen tank in one of the ambulances was nowhere to be found.
Upsound Rolene some of the stories move me to tears as well, and so I can understand that when you passionately want to provide a view based, you need the tools of the trade to do so. And we've made an undertaking, and I've been quite unequivocal as the accounting officer. If they are reporting it and it is not being attended to, they must please escalate it and they will be assisted.
V/O Mzamane is one of more than 200 members of the National Education, Health, and Allied Workers' Union who, for the last 4 months, have been reporting for duty… but have not been responding to emergency calls…as a protest.
V/O Under cover of darkness, they invite us to join a night shift in the small town of Alice - 20 KM away from Fort Beaufort.
V/O I am met by a shocking sight
Mac Link : These are some of the working and living conditions some of the guys are complaining about , I mean if you look at this place, it's unbelievable that they have no place to relax and no place to rest while they are waiting for calls
V/O Workers here tell me that three of their five ambulances are idle… and the other two have just come back from a repair workshop… and are still not equipped, making them useless.
Mac Link: The idea was to hang out with emergency service workers, see the pressures and conditions that they and it doesnt look like its going to happen because the area we have doesn't have network, you cant get any cellphone communication and the press and talk also doesnt work.
V/O These devices rely on patchy networks in the area.
Mac : People might say you are being selfish and putting people’s lives at risk
Upsound Mzamane EMS worker When you take an empty ambulance you have to write a statement as to why the patient has died and it remains to be seen whether you are charged or not.
MAKE A MORE GENTLE SEGUE –
Up sound Phathelwa : He got sick in May and they told me the ambulances are on strike. I had to hire a car to take him to the hospital.
V/O This situation has left many chronically ill patients like Mthetheli Majombolwana and his sister , also his caregiver Phathelwa in crisis
Upsound Phathelwa : We took him to Port Alfred hospital, that’s when they found a brain tumour. Thats what led to his blindness .He was too weak, and he couldn't even walk
Upsound Phathelwa : It scares me, What if he were to die . Seizers can lead to death, it scares me.
V/O Shockingly Mzamane alleges that in trying to meet the Quality assurance test to declare their ambulances fit for service delivery, the department of health is cutting corners
Upsound Mzamane The reason that we are in this situation is that the department and installed equipment in the ambulances, they took pictures and showed us that this is the sort of equipment ambulances should have. After that, they took out the equipment.
Mac : Why do they take it out
Mac: The allegations that are on the ground are that ambulances, officers with the equipment past been removed and taken to another ambulance and another on so that they can look like they have been certified to be able to be operational. For me, that is fraud.
Upsound Rolene :I view it, as fraud as well, we've directed that an investigation be launched to determine how this licensing how the licensing exercise was done. And if there was fraud, we definitely will hold them. There will be consequences that will follow. At the same time, when we did ask the explanation that was given was that the equipment is put into the vehicle, but there isn't enough space to store all of the equipment in the vehicle, all because of the risk of theft.
V/O Wagner insists she will revive Emergency care in the Eastern Cape.
Upsound Roelene : Our plan is for the next ten years to systematically address all of the gaps that we have within EMS.
V/O but until then people like Mthetheli and Nosintu will have to make other… expensive and often risky plans… when seeking critical emergency care.
-end–




Upsound Mzamane EMS worker There is no oxygen, those are the splints…So you open the windows so that the person can get air from the window.
Upsound Phumzile: People are dying whilst there are ambulances.
